column7: The "holy catholic Church" refers to the universal body of Christ, comprising all believers across time and space. The Church is set apart for God’s purposes, called to reflect His holiness and share the gospel. The "communion of saints" emphasizes the unity of all Christians, living and dead, as members of Christ’s body (Ephesians 4:4-6). This fellowship transcends earthly divisions, demonstrating the shared hope and mission of believers.
column8: The phrase "the holy universal Church" refers to the global body of Christ, composed of all believers in every time and place. The Church is devoted to God’s purposes and is called to display his holiness and share the Gospel. The phrase "the communion of saints" emphasizes the unity of all Christians, both the living and the dead, as members of the body of Christ (Ephesians 4:4-6). This fellowship transcends worldly divisions, displaying the shared hope and mission of believers.
